instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Fair Exchange
cards.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sorted the chores fairly. I wash this pan; you owe me two shopping trips.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two trips for one pan? That's not fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dried cheese is a premium job. But I want us both happy with the arrangement. What would you offer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll soak it first. Then it just needs a wipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A prepared-pan rate, naturally. One shopping trip, and you supply the detergent. You choose the day; I'll mark us settled when the shopping's home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll coordinate our exchange. Half an hour helping you move gets me two hours of shed painting Saturday morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Morning's my only lie-in. I can come after lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'd miss cricket. Three hours for the afternoon slot. Unless you've a way to keep both our plans intact?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But the sofa needs carrying up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That works with my system. Two painter-hours for loading, one for the stairs. You choose the painter and day; I'll fit the shed around them. Cricket stays mine.

cards.title: Technically, Yes
cards.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've handled your moving request. You said move a box, and that one is beside the van. Completely done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant all twenty boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All twenty beside the van, certainly. You can choose the order; I'll work around you. That's the full revised request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Inside the van, with the labels facing the doors so I can read them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Every label facing the doors. You choose the rows; I'll stack them that way. You can read the back row first and unload it to see the next. Every label accessible, in order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've managed the holiday watering. The fern you pointed at has had water; your request is complete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every plant, every day until Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. A teaspoon each, daily. You choose the time; I'll fit the round around it. Every plant covered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A full can each. And I want those saucers empty when I get home Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A full can, agreed. Tell me your arrival time and I'll empty them just before it. Daily watering, saucers empty on your return: every word taken care of.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll manage this tap repair properly. The drip gives us a reason to replace the sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, we'll use yours. While the sink's out, I'll replace the swollen worktop. You choose the finish; I want you happy with it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can finally fix the layout. You sketch where you'd like the cupboards; I'll arrange to empty the whole kitchen. We won't waste the chance your washer has opened up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the cafe before we open. That chair wobbles; let's dismantle the chairs and check the joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I checked. It's just that floorboard. The chairs are fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good testing. We'll keep the chairs and lift the boards. Tell me which area you want clear first; I'll work around you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We open in twenty minutes. I need the counter accessible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll close for renovations and move the counter somewhere better. You choose where service should start; I'll plan the new queue around it. Much easier once the floor's up.

cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make Them Your Deputy
cards.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need you running the raffle table as my deputy. I've made the badge; I'll direct the draw.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not co-organizer? I know more about the prizes than you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then prizes are your department. Choose them all, and I'll introduce you as my deputy in charge of prizes. How does that sound?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to announce the winners too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll give you the signal for each draw, and you can announce every winner in your own style. I'll stand beside you and make sure everyone knows you're the deputy doing the work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come organize the picnic as my second-in-command. I'll give you the shopping instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm happy to shop, but I'm not ringing you from every aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll issue one clear list and you choose the shop. A good deputy needs room to work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And if they haven't got what you listed, I'm choosing the replacements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose them. Just show me the bags before we set out and I'll check the picnic supplies are ready. One report at the end, not twenty phone calls. That's the direction I'll give you.

cards.title: Not Dismissed
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shop's closed. Wait at the till until I dismiss you; I'll finish the evening properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've counted it. My daughter's waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll do your dismissal by the door. You can stand with her; I want this comfortable for everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our taxi's here. I'm putting her in it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll walk as far as you want me to. Once she's settled, look back and I'll give you the nod to leave. You choose the pace; I still need to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll formally conclude our coffee before you go. Keep your coat off until I release you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My bus is due. I'm putting it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, prepared departure. Choose the seat nearest the door and I'll make my decision there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cafe's closing. They've told us both to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll do this walking toward your stop. You set the pace; I'll keep up. When I say you're free to go, you can stop matching my stride.
